what_its_for: Nizatidine is used to treat and prevent heartburn, acid indigestion, and sour stomach. It is also used to treat ulcers in the stomach and small intestine, and a condition called gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), where stomach acid backs up into the throat.
how_to_take: Take nizatidine by mouth with or without food. Swallow the capsule whole with a full glass of water. If you are using the liquid form, measure your dose carefully with a measuring spoon or cup — do not use a regular kitchen spoon. You can take the over-the-counter version about 30 to 60 minutes before eating foods or drinking drinks that may cause heartburn.
dosing: For heartburn prevention (over-the-counter): The usual adult dose is 75 mg taken once or twice daily, no more than 2 tablets in 24 hours, and for no longer than 2 weeks unless your doctor tells you otherwise. For ulcers or GERD (prescription): Your doctor will set the right dose for you, which is commonly 150 mg twice a day or 300 mg once at bedtime. Always follow your doctor's or pharmacist's instructions exactly.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store nizatidine at room temperature, away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Keep it out of the bathroom medicine cabinet. Keep all medications out of the reach of children and pets. Do not use the medication past its expiration date — check the label and discard properly.
what_to_avoid: Avoid foods and drinks that can make heartburn or stomach acid worse, such as spicy foods, fatty or fried foods, chocolate, caffeine, alcohol, citrus fruits, and tomato-based products. Avoid smoking, as it can increase stomach acid. Avoid lying down right after eating. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before taking antacids at the same time as nizatidine, as timing may need to be adjusted.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: trouble swallowing or painful swallowing, vomiting blood or material that looks like coffee grounds, black or tarry stools, unexplained weight loss, chest pain, severe stomach pain, yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), dark urine, unusual bruising or bleeding, confusion or mood changes, or signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also call your doctor if your heartburn does not improve after 2 weeks of over-the-counter use.
when_it_works: Nizatidine usually starts to relieve heartburn symptoms within 30 minutes to 1 hour after taking a dose. For ulcer healing or GERD treatment, it may take several days to a few weeks of regular use before you feel the full benefit. Keep taking the medication as directed, even if you start to feel better, unless your doctor tells you to stop.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and older): Older adults may be more sensitive to the effects of nizatidine and may need a lower dose. Talk to your doctor. Kidney problems: If you have kidney disease, your doctor may need to lower your dose because nizatidine is removed from the body by the kidneys. Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before using nizatidine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Breastfeeding: Nizatidine may pass into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before using it while breastfeeding. Children: Prescription nizatidine may be used in children under a doctor's supervision, but the over-the-counter version is generally for adults only.
